findings.title: Off-by-one error in totalPages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example, 50 members with the default limit of 50), this returns `2` instead of `1`. Consequently `showingLast` (`currentPage === totalPages`) is false on the last real page, allowing the user to click "Next" to an empty page where `offset` equals `user_count`. It should use `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

findings.title: Admin::GroupsController#create ignores alias_level parameter
findings.body: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` when creating a new group via `POST /admin/groups`, and the admin group form allows selecting an `alias_level` before saving a new group. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`. Any alias level chosen when creating a group is silently discarded and has to be set again in a subsequent update.

findings.title: GroupsController#members allows unbounded or negative limit and offset
findings.body: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to ActiveRecord `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` without bounds checking. A client can pass a very large `limit` (e.g. `limit=1000000`) to load and serialize all users in a large group in one request, or pass a negative `limit`/`offset` which causes PostgreSQL to raise an `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`LIMIT must not be negative` / `OFFSET must not be negative`) resulting in an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: Adding an already-present member in add_members raises a uniqueness constraint error
findings.body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (`group.users.push(user)`) is called for each username without checking whether the user is already a member of the group. `GroupUser` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)`, so if any of the submitted usernames is already in the group (or if the same username appears twice in `usernames`), `group.add(user)` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500 error instead of skipping existing members.
